about.text: Hard cheese ripened a year or more, until it is dry enough to break into grains and to grate rather than slice: under 51 % water in the cheese without its fat, as the Codex standard has it. Parmigiano Reggiano, Grana Padano, Sbrinz and Pecorino Romano are among them.

picks.why: The archetype of extra-hard grana cheese, a PDO made in Emilia-Romagna since the Middle Ages and copied worldwide.
Italy's most produced PDO cheese and the other defining grana of the Po Valley.
The oldest of Italy's great grating cheeses, a salty sheep's-milk PDO from Lazio and Sardinia, exported widely.
Switzerland's extra-hard PDO cheese, aged up to thirty months and grated or shaved in Swiss cooking.
Argentina's well-known answer to Parmigiano, made by Italian immigrants and the leading extra-hard cheese outside Europe.
